```{r setup, include=FALSE}
                      warning = FALSE, error = FALSE, cache = FALSE)

library(MetaQCAT)
data("CRC_data", package = "MetaQCAT")
data("IBD_data", package = "MetaQCAT")
```

# Scope and interface

MetaQCAT combines covariate-adjusted score summaries across independent studies.
The count component tests the composition of child taxa **conditional on the
total count within the specified lineage**, not total family abundance in the
microbiome. The zero component tests observed-zero indicators, not verified
biological absence. The public calibration in version 0.2.1 is a null-imposed
wild-score bootstrap; labels and covariates are not permuted.

| Method | Component | Returned calibration |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `FE-MetaQCAT` | Count composition | `Asy`, `Boot` |
| `FE-MetaQCAT*` | Observed-zero pattern | `Asy`, `Boot` |
| `FE-MetaQCAT-O` | Cauchy combination of count and zero p-values | `Asy`, `Boot` |
| `RE-MetaQCAT` | Count composition with a heterogeneity score | `Boot` |
| `RE-MetaQCAT*` | Zero pattern with a heterogeneity score | `Boot` |
| `RE-MetaQCAT-O` | Cauchy combination of the RE component p-values | `Boot` |

`X` contains the exposure and adjustment variables without an intercept.
`X.index` identifies the column(s) to test; all other columns remain nuisance
covariates. Adjustment sets can differ across studies, but tested coefficient
meanings and ordering must agree. For within-subject or between-subject effects,
construct the appropriate columns explicitly: the package does not decompose
exposures automatically. This is why there is no within/between permutation
option. `n.boot = 999L` replaces the old `n.perm` interface.

# Null-imposed score bootstrap

For each lineage, component and study, the covariate-adjusted null is fitted
once. Write $s_{\beta,\ell i}$ and $s_{\gamma,\ell i}$ for the tested and nuisance
scores summed over visits of independent subject $i$. With total sensitivity
blocks evaluated under the null,

\[
u_{\ell i}=s_{\beta,\ell i}-H_{\beta\gamma,\ell}
 H_{\gamma\gamma,\ell}^{-1}s_{\gamma,\ell i},\qquad
J_\ell=H_{\beta\beta,\ell}-H_{\beta\gamma,\ell}
 H_{\gamma\gamma,\ell}^{-1}H_{\gamma\beta,\ell}.
\]

The rows of $\Psi_\ell$ are $\psi_{\ell i}^{T}$, where
$\psi_{\ell i}=J_\ell^{-1}u_{\ell i}$. They are **not centered**.
The one-step score summary and unscaled sandwich covariance are
$\widehat\beta_\ell=\sum_i\psi_{\ell i}$ and
$V_\ell=\Psi_\ell^T\Psi_\ell$. These are null-based score summaries;
they are not full-model coefficient fits under arbitrary alternatives.

Each bootstrap draw independently assigns a Rademacher multiplier
$\xi_{\ell i}\in\{-1,+1\}$ to each subject, and forms
$\widehat\beta_\ell^*=\Psi_\ell^T\xi_\ell$. The observed summary is **not** added.
Sensitivity matrices, covariances, kernels, retained taxa, references and any
completed rarefaction remain fixed. Conditional on the data, bootstrap mean is
zero and covariance is $V_\ell$. No nuisance fit is repeated inside a draw.
Reduced models use ordinary maximum-likelihood nuisance estimates; convergence
and nuisance-score residuals are checked rather than silently replacing the
ordinary score equations with a bias-reduced fit.

Multipliers are keyed by study and subject and reused across count, zero,
FE, RE and lineage calculations. Excluding a subject from one component does
not shift another subject's weights. Independent samples are subjects of size
one. Named studies and stable sample/subject identifiers are needed for
reordering-invariant reproducibility; positional identifiers cannot establish
identity after an arbitrary row permutation.

Count RE uses $B_\ell=(I_{K_\ell}+\mathbf1\mathbf1^T)\otimes I_q$ in taxon-major
ALR coordinates and adds $\{\max(0,U)\}^2/I_\sigma$ to FE after summing the variance
score across studies. The zero RE component retains its own identity kernel
and uses the same positive-part boundary convention after summing its variance
score across studies.
Observed and bootstrap statistics use the same evaluator and cached matrices.
The count reference-invariance property requires the same eligible taxa/studies,
harmonized coordinates and nonsingular information/covariances. Unsupported
rank or conditioning returns a documented failure, not a silent ridge or
pseudoinverse.

The marginal p-value is
\[
p=\frac{1+\sum_{r=1}^{R}1\{Q_r^*\ge Q_{\rm obs}\}}{R+1},\qquad R=\texttt{n.boot}.
\]
All requested draws run; ties count as exceedances. Nonfinite draws are errors,
not deleted observations. The `-O` tests apply the existing equal-weight Cauchy
rule to the **marginal** bootstrap p-values, with documented endpoint handling.
The plus-one marginal bootstrap p-values are positive; a component p-value of
one gives a combined value of one. For asymptotic p-values, zero gives zero
unless a zero and one occur together; that mixed boundary pair is clipped at
$10^{-15}$ and $1-10^{-15}$ before combination. Other values use a numerically
stable Cauchy-tail calculation.
They are not a separately joint-bootstrap-calibrated omnibus. Validate both
omnibus tests separately before claiming calibration. BH adjustment is applied
to the prespecified eligible family; failed analyses are retained as `NA` and
their frequency must be reported.

This construction adapts [Kline and Santos (2012)](https://doi.org/10.1515/2156-6674.1006)
and nuisance-adjusted sign-flipping principles of
[Hemerik, Goeman and Finos (2020)](https://doi.org/10.1111/rssb.12369).
It is asymptotic, not finite-sample exact. Valid null estimating equations,
regular nuisance estimation, independent clusters, finite moments, no dominant
cluster and stable full-rank matrices are required. It does not fix unmeasured
confounding, arbitrary mean-model misspecification or participants shared across
nominally independent studies. Those references do not establish a published
proof of this complete RE/Cauchy workflow.

# Independent-sample example

This small synthetic example executes during vignette checks. Nineteen draws
are for software demonstration only, not discovery analysis.

```{r independent-example}
set.seed(31)
counts <- X <- vector("list", 2L)
names(counts) <- names(X) <- c("Study_A", "Study_B")
for (s in seq_along(counts)) {
  counts[[s]] <- t(rmultinom(80L, 80L, c(.4, .35, .25)))
  dimnames(counts[[s]]) <- list(paste0("sample_", 1:80), paste0("taxon_", 1:3))
  X[[s]] <- cbind(disease = rep(0:1, 40L), age = rnorm(80L))
  rownames(X[[s]]) <- rownames(counts[[s]])
}
fit <- MetaQCAT(counts, X, X.index = 1L, method = "FE-MetaQCAT",
                min.prev = 0, n.boot = 19L, seed = 42L)
fit$pvalue.comp
fit$bootstrap
```

For the packaged CRC data, `CRC_data$disease` is the original unadjusted design.
To adjust for other covariates, explicitly construct and verify a complete
`X` list; metadata fields alone do not imply adjustment.

```{r crc-template, eval=FALSE}
tax <- CRC_data$taxonomy[, c("Rank5", "Rank6"), drop = FALSE]
colnames(tax) <- c("Rank1", "Rank2")
crc_fit <- MetaQCAT(CRC_data$counts, CRC_data$disease, X.index = 1L,
  taxonomy = tax, method = "FE-MetaQCAT-O", n.boot = 9999L, seed = 2026L)
saveRDS(crc_fit, "CRC_FE_omnibus.rds")
```

# Repeated-sample IBD example

The packaged IBD data use nonoverlapping analysis strata and explicit subject
IDs. The first design column is disease; other columns are adjustment variables.
Check source cohort overlap for any replacement data before analysis.

```{r ibd-template, eval=FALSE}
tax <- IBD_data$taxonomy[, c("Rank5", "Rank6"), drop = FALSE]
colnames(tax) <- c("Rank1", "Rank2")
ibd_fit <- MetaQCAT(IBD_data$counts, IBD_data$design, X.index = 1L,
  cluster.id = IBD_data$subject_ids, taxonomy = tax,
  method = "RE-MetaQCAT-O", n.boot = 9999L, min.prev = c(.1, .1),
  seed = 2026L, n.threads = 4L)
saveRDS(ibd_fit, "IBD_RE_omnibus.rds")
```

# Reporting and validation

Save the entire results object and the source configuration. Report seed,
package and dependency versions, preprocessing, independent-cluster counts,
requested/completed draws, eligibility and failure reasons. A taxonomy scan
returns `lineage.pval`, `lineage.qval`, `lineage.coef`, `sig.lineage` and
`failed.lineage`; its bootstrap rows begin `Bootstrap-`. Failed lineages retain
their names and `NA` columns. `save.coef` retains score summaries when requested.
Bootstrap metadata records calibration, multiplier/covariance conventions,
the RNG triplet, stable subject IDs, requested/completed repetitions and
per-lineage completion counts.
The p-value floor is $1/(R+1)$; assess it against the intended BH thresholds.
Use matched, prespecified budgets for full and cohort-omission fits.

Opt-in scripts under `inst/validation` cover independent/repeated samples,
covariate-balanced/associated disease, sample-size convergence, representative
power and full-pipeline stress settings. They record all six tests, p-values,
rejection rates at 0.05/0.01, binomial Monte Carlo intervals, attempted and failed
fits, timing, configuration and session information. They do not run during
`R CMD check`. Small smoke runs check execution only: large calibration,
application reruns and global/mixed-null omnibus-plus-BH simulations remain
necessary before corresponding accuracy or FDR claims. No planned experiment
should be reported as completed.
